newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice closes lower on harvest and weaker cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice closes lower on harvest and weaker cash.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed lower on increased harvesting of the U.S. rice crop and a weak tone to the cash rice market, traders said.
"In reality the good harvest is weighing on the market," a trader said. Also "traders are expecting deliveries (on the Sep) tomorrow."

The fact the U.S. cash market remains at a premium to Asian values, signs Brazil will not be an aggressive buyer of U.S. rice and an increase by USDA in its estimate for U.S. rice production also weighed on the market. USDA said U.S. rice outturn this year would be 171.5 million cwt.
That tally was above the August forecast for 168.8 milllion cwt.
Rice futures volume was estimated at 200 contracts, up from 180 Tuesday, according to the CBOT. Rice options volume was estimated at 10 contracts, down from 20 Tuesday.
Rice futures closed one to three cents per cwt lower, with September down one at $10.25 per cwt.
